questions.q: What is the main difference in scope between a Salesforce Admin and an Application Architect, per this lesson?
options: An Admin configures a single org to match a process; an Application Architect decides what kind of application and platform capabilities should solve the problem and how it should be structured to survive change
There is no real difference — both roles do the same work with different titles
An Admin only works in sandboxes, while an Application Architect only works in production
An Application Architect writes all the Apex code, while an Admin never touches code
questions.explain: The Admin executes configuration; the Application Architect makes the upstream design decisions — what to build it from and how to structure it — that the Admin and Developer then build inside.

questions.q: Which four certifications does Salesforce require as prerequisites for the Application Architect credential?
options: Marketing Cloud Administrator, Service Cloud Consultant, Sales Cloud Consultant, CPQ Specialist
Platform App Builder, Platform Developer I, Data Architect, Sharing and Visibility Architect
System Architect, Integration Architect, Identity and Access Management Architect, Development Lifecycle Architect
Administrator, Advanced Administrator, Platform App Builder, Platform Developer II
questions.explain: Application Architect assumes you already hold Platform App Builder, Platform Developer I, Data Architect, and Sharing and Visibility Architect, then tests whether you can combine those skills into one coherent application design.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe the relationship between Application Architect, System Architect, and Technical Architect (CTA)?
options: Application Architect and System Architect are two parallel credentials that, combined, are a major step toward the capstone Technical Architect credential
Technical Architect is a prerequisite for Application Architect, not the other way around
System Architect replaces the need for Application Architect entirely
The three credentials cover completely unrelated skill sets with no overlap
questions.explain: Application Architect (data/sharing/app design) and System Architect (integration/DevOps/environments) are parallel, and holding both is explicitly framed as a major step toward the review-board-gated Technical Architect (CTA) credential.

questions.q: What is explicitly out of scope for this course, according to this lesson?
options: Entire multi-org, multi-cloud enterprise architecture (Technical Architect scope) and deep large-data-volume/sharing-model design (prerequisite Data Architect and Sharing and Visibility Architect skills)
Anything involving Apex code
Anything involving Lightning pages
Nothing is out of scope — this course covers every architect credential
questions.explain: This course stays scoped to a single application's architecture, assuming you already have the prerequisite data-volume and sharing-model skills, and does not extend into the enterprise-wide, multi-org scope of the Technical Architect credential.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why does the Application Architect role matter even when a solution 'already works'?
options: Because working and well-architected are different bars — a solution can function today and still be unmaintainable, unscalable, or hard to extend later
Because a solution that works is automatically well-architected by definition
Because the Application Architect's only job is performance tuning after launch
Because working solutions never need an architect's involvement
questions.explain: The lesson frames 'it works' and 'it's well-architected' as separate bars — a design can function in the short term while still creating long-term maintainability, scalability, or extensibility problems the Application Architect exists to catch early.
